title: The Sunk Cost Trap: Why You Keep Feeding Dead Projects

scenes.narration: Your past effort is already goneâ€”you can never get it back. The only real question is whether you will sacrifice your future just to justify what you already spent.
This is the sunk cost fallacy. Because you poured two years or ten thousand dollars into a leaking bucket, your brain convinces you to keep pouring even more into a dead project.
Instead of an investment, your past commitment turns into an iron anchor chained to your ankleâ€”dragging down your energy, your calendar, and every new opportunity you could be building.
Most people do not stay because they believe in the project. They stay because walking away feels like admitting defeat, and ego hates looking wrong.
Here is the simplest test to break the spell instantly. Ask yourself: knowing everything I know today, if I were not already in this, would I start it from scratch?
If the honest answer is no, cut the rope today. Not next quarter, not after one more try. Strategic quitting is not weaknessâ€”it is precision.
The exact second you drop dead weight, you feel an immediate surge of buoyancy. Your time returns, your mind clears, and your best work finally has room to rise.
Never stay loyal to a mistake just because you spent a long time making it. Honor your futureâ€”not your sunk costs.
